title: Devcontainer becomes a full builder image
summary: This change turns the devcontainer from a minimal Rust image into the full factory builder image: it pins and installs moon, Node 22, pnpm, Bun, gh, actionlint, uv, SkillSpector/SkillEvaluator, the four coding agents (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp) and dsh, builds the dsh/omp/opencode integrations from the workspace pnpm lockfile, wires every agent's hook files root-owned and read-only, replaces the system-wide core.hooksPath with a git wrapper that forces the hooks path per call, and adds a suite of build-time tests that prove the wrapper, hooks, toolchain read-only-ness and image cleanliness.

lanes.label: Image build
lanes.subtitle: Dockerfile layers
lanes.summary: The Dockerfile stages that fetch, verify and install every tool, then lock them down root-owned.

lanes.label: Container runtime
lanes.subtitle: dev user, /workspace
lanes.summary: What the dev user actually gets at run time: PATH, workspace mount, agents, hooks and the git wrapper.

lanes.label: Factory tooling
lanes.subtitle: osf, moon, pnpm workspace
lanes.summary: The osf binary, moon task runner and the pnpm workspace whose integrations are built into the image.

lanes.label: External sources
lanes.subtitle: release tarballs, npm, git
lanes.summary: Everything the build downloads: pinned release assets, npm packages and git commits.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Grows from a Rust-only image into the full builder image: pinned ARGs and SHA-256 checks for every tool, uv-installed skill checkers, Node/pnpm/Bun, the four coding agents, dsh from its own lockfile, the pnpm workspace build, hook wiring, and a chain of build-time test scripts.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount /workspace
nodes.summary: Now pins the bind mount target to /workspace, forwards GH_TOKEN from the host, and its postCreateCommand checks osf, moon, node and pnpm and reports that no local core.hooksPath is set.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, and now forces core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for every git call under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT instead of relying on a system-wide setting.

nodes.label: git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Root-owned, read-only hook scripts that each call osf. Unchanged in content; what changed is how they are reached, via the wrapper rather than /etc/gitconfig.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: The factory CLI, built from the workspace and installed root-owned and read-only. It is the single thing every hook and every agent hook file calls.

nodes.label: osf hooks install
nodes.subtitle: --agents --root
nodes.summary: Writes each agent's hook files from the [agents] table of osf.toml. The Dockerfile runs it at build time, then chowns the written files root-owned and read-only, and copies the claude and opencode ones to system-wide paths.

nodes.label: moon
nodes.summary: The task runner every factory check goes through. Moved from /opt/factory/bin to /usr/local/bin and now installed before the osf build rather than after.

nodes.label: pnpm workspace
nodes.subtitle: apps, packages, integrations
nodes.summary: The workspace whose lockfile the image builds from, so the dsh, omp and opencode integrations ship with exactly the dependency versions CI already tests.

nodes.label: dsh integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/dsh
nodes.summary: The dsh writing-check plugin. Its package.json and index.ts changed, and its built dist is copied into both the factory and headless dsh profiles under the dev home.

nodes.label: omp integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/omp
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace and installed under the dev home's node_modules as @open-software-factory/osf-omp-hook, where node resolves it for omp's hook file.

nodes.label: opencode integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/opencode
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace and installed under the dev home's node_modules as @open-software-factory/osf-opencode-plugin.

nodes.label: dsh package
nodes.subtitle: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: A dedicated npm project with its own lockfile, installed with npm ci into /opt/dsh and symlinked onto PATH as dsh.

nodes.label: coding agents
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude-code, opencode, omp
nodes.summary: Four global npm installs, each pinned to one exact version, all usable as builder or reviewer. omp runs on Bun, which is why Bun is installed too.

nodes.label: agent hook files
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude, opencode, omp, dsh
nodes.summary: Each agent's own hook settings, root-owned and read-only, calling osf hook for the stop and prompt events it supports. Codex's live under /etc/codex; claude's and opencode's are copied to system-wide paths; omp's and dsh's stay under the dev home.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: prompt, stop
nodes.summary: The command every agent hook file invokes. It has no pre-tool-use event, which is why none is wired.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: /etc/profile.d
nodes.summary: Restores PATH in login shells, which otherwise reset it before reading profile.d and drop osf, cargo and every agent binary.

nodes.label: build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 9 scripts
nodes.summary: git-wrapper, git-hooks, agent-hooks, skills-installed, dsh-starts, coding-agent-tools, builder-tools, toolchain-readonly and image-clean each run during the build so a broken image fails the build instead of shipping.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image workflow
nodes.subtitle: .github/workflows
nodes.summary: A new workflow that builds the devcontainer image, so the Dockerfile changes are exercised in CI rather than only on a developer's machine.

nodes.label: release tarballs
nodes.subtitle: moon, gh, actionlint, uv, node, bun
nodes.summary: Every binary comes from its own GitHub or nodejs.org release asset, checked against a pinned SHA-256 per architecture.

nodes.label: npm registry
nodes.subtitle: agents, dsh, skills CLI
nodes.summary: The coding agents, dsh and the skills CLI are installed from npm at exact pinned versions.

nodes.label: skill repos
nodes.subtitle: NVIDIA, archify
nodes.summary: SkillSpector and SkillEvaluator are installed from NVIDIA git commits, and the archify skills from a pinned archify commit, never vendored.

edges.label: npm install -g
edges.summary: The build installs all four coding agents as global npm packages into the root-owned Node install, then strips group and other write bits.

edges.label: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
edges.summary: A second build directory outside /workspace installs the workspace from the lockfile and builds the dsh, omp and opencode integrations.

edges.label: npm ci
edges.summary: dsh is installed from its own lockfile into /opt/dsh and symlinked onto PATH.

edges.label: osf hooks install --agents
edges.summary: The build runs osf hooks install against a copy of osf.toml, then chowns each written file root-owned and read-only.

edges.label: sh <test>.sh
edges.summary: Nine test scripts run inside the build, each proving one property of the finished image.

edges.label: COPY, chmod 0555
edges.summary: The wrapper is copied in root-owned and read-only, and the system-wide core.hooksPath line it replaces is removed.
The profile.d script is copied in root-owned and read-only so login shells keep their PATH.
moon moves from /opt/factory/bin to /usr/local/bin and is installed earlier in the build.

edges.label: cargo build --release
edges.summary: osf is still built from the workspace and installed root-owned and read-only at /opt/factory/bin/osf.

edges.label: curl + sha256sum -c
edges.summary: Each tool is fetched from its release URL and verified against a pinned per-architecture checksum before install.
npm installs the agents, dsh and the skills CLI at exact pinned versions.

edges.label: uv tool install git+https
edges.summary: SkillSpector and SkillEvaluator come from pinned NVIDIA commits; the archify skills come from a pinned archify commit via the skills CLI.

edges.label: /workspace bind mount
edges.summary: devcontainer.json pins the bind mount to /workspace, the same path OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT names, so the wrapper's workspace test matches the mount.

edges.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
edges.summary: The wrapper now passes the hooks path on the command line for every git call under the workspace, replacing the system-wide core.hooksPath that used to apply to every repository including test scratch repos.
Each hook script calls osf; the wrapper is what guarantees they run.

edges.label: wrote <path>
edges.summary: osf hooks install prints one 'wrote <path>' line per file; the Dockerfile parses those lines to chown and chmod each file root-owned and read-only.

edges.label: osf hook prompt
edges.summary: Every agent hook file invokes osf hook for the prompt event, and for the stop event where the agent has one.

edges.label: dist copied into profiles
edges.summary: The built dsh plugin dist is copied into the factory and headless profile node_modules, and each profile's cordis.patch.yml registers it.

edges.label: node_modules/@open-software-factory
edges.summary: The built omp package is installed under the dev home's node_modules so omp's hook file can resolve it by name.

edges.label: node_modules/@open-software-factory
edges.summary: The built opencode plugin is installed under the dev home's node_modules for the same reason.
git-wrapper.sh proves the refusals and the forced hooks path at build time.
git-hooks.sh proves the hooks are executable, that every osf flag they use exists, and that each runs in a scratch repository.
agent-hooks.sh reads the [agents] table and proves every enabled agent's hook file is root-owned and read-only and that osf hook answers a sample payload.
coding-agent-tools.sh and builder-tools.sh prove each agent and builder tool runs for the dev user, including from a login shell.
dsh-starts.sh proves dsh starts on both profiles with no credentials and stops only at the missing credential.
The new workflow builds the devcontainer image in CI, exercising the Dockerfile changes.

flows.title: An agent prompt reaches osf hook
flows.summary: What happens when a developer submits a prompt to any of the four coding agents: the agent's own hook file, installed root-owned and read-only at build time, invokes osf hook, which is the same binary the git hooks call.

messages.label: UserPromptSubmit
messages.note: Each agent reads its own hook settings: codex from /etc/codex, claude and opencode from their system-wide copies, omp and dsh from the dev home.

messages.label: osf hook prompt
messages.note: The hook file is root-owned and read-only, so the command it runs cannot be repointed by the dev user.

messages.label: exit status
messages.note: osf hook has no pre-tool-use event, so only prompt and stop are ever wired.

flows.title: A git commit under /workspace
flows.summary: How a commit made by the dev user reaches the factory hooks now that the system-wide core.hooksPath is gone: the wrapper decides the repository is under the workspace and forces the hooks path on the command line.

messages.label: git commit
messages.note: The wrapper checks the repository path against OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT before deciding whether to force the hooks path.

messages.label: --no-verify / -n refused
messages.note: The refusal behaviour is unchanged; what changed is that the hooks path is now forced per call rather than set system-wide.

messages.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Because the path is passed on the command line, a scratch repository under /tmp with no local override is no longer forced to use the factory hooks.
